chosen_leak: Claim page: landed → gave email (the QR-scan email gate; ~40% capture, ~57–60% lost, ~115 people per fortnight)
why_highest_impact: This is the single largest drop in the funnel by headcount AND it sits at the very top, so everything downstream multiplies off it. Trace to REVIEWS: an email is the ONLY key that unlocks both review-producing engines — (1) it delivers the code+video, funnelling the person toward the in-app thank-you screen that today produces almost ALL in-app review clicks, and (2) it enrolls them in Klaviyo, whose reminder Emails 5/6 produce a real, separate share of review clicks (phase=email_redirect). Every other leak is DOWNSTREAM of this one and can only act on the ~40% who got through. The in-app 'arrived→started video' leak (~60% of warm users) was genuinely attacked twice recently (2026-06-16 hero bundle = worked; 2026-07-06 message-friction = shipped), so it is recently-touched; the preview/share review asks (~0%) and the in-app thank-you screen are lower total-review contributors and the thank-you screen just drew an owner rejection (2026-07-22). By contrast the email gate is the biggest, feeds reviews on two paths, and has had only ONE real conversion attempt (PR #8, a layout/hierarchy rebuild that went flat) plus one owner-rejected idea (discount-first); everything since (2026-07-20, 2026-07-22) was measurement-only, which does not count as trying. The owner's 2026-07-22 rejection explicitly asked us to attack a bigger, un-tried leak — this is it.

angles.mechanism: Open the page by completing the emotional beat the box started ('did this potato make you smile?') in the same warm voice, acknowledging the gift/the smile BEFORE stating the reward — so the visitor stays in the delighted mindset that made them pull out a phone and scan, instead of hitting a cold coupon-form header and pattern-matching 'marketing form → bounce'. It keeps the emotional thread continuous from box → page so more people lean in and engage the field at all.
angles.cause_addressed: Thin motivation / tonal break: the box that MADE them scan is warm and playful; the page greets that warmth with a transactional 'You've Got 30% Off / Enter your email to receive / Send Me My Code'. The emotional pull evaporates before they engage.
angles.evidence_hint: Session replays show ~67% never type a single key — the loss is overwhelmingly at 'never engaged', not form friction. The box voice is documented as warm/playful; the current hero is transactional. Points to people not feeling pulled in at first paint.
angles.why_untried_and_different: PR #8 rebuilt LAYOUT/HIERARCHY (structure) and went flat; this touches the opening VOICE/first line, a motivation mechanism, not a reshuffle of the same elements. It is not the discount-first rejection and never references the printed percentage.
angles.on_brand_fit: It IS the brand voice — warm, human, playful-but-refined; maximally on-brand, no emoji soup, no push.
angles.size: SMALL: rewrite the kicker + reward-intro copy (one headline + one subhead) in claim.html; no layout, fully reversible.

angles.mechanism: Add a gentle, truthful cue that their code is set aside and waiting for them right now (not a fake countdown) — giving a reason to finish the email in THIS session rather than mentally deferring it and never returning. Turns a single-visit 'I'll do it later' into 'I'll do it now'.
angles.cause_addressed: No reason to act NOW: this is a one-visit funnel with no scarcity or timeliness; people intend to claim later and never come back.
angles.evidence_hint: The claim funnel is effectively single-session (QR scan, no return path), and ~67% leave without acting — the classic signature of no-urgency drift. Unsettled on magnitude — a bet.
angles.why_untried_and_different: The page has ZERO urgency mechanism today (grep confirms no expire/reserved/limited/today copy). Never attempted; distinct from PR #8's structure work and unrelated to the rejected discount-first / printed-% ideas.
angles.on_brand_fit: Must stay warm and honest (reserved/waiting, not 'HURRY 10:00 LEFT'); framed as care, not pressure — keeps the premium, non-pushy bar.
angles.size: SMALL: one honest line near the CTA in claim.html; no timer infra, reversible.

angles.mechanism: Replace the generic trust bar ('No spam, ever / Code sent by email / Unsubscribe anytime') with a small, concrete signal that this is the genuine handmade shop behind the gift — the maker/brand identity and a light proof-of-realness — so a suspicious scanner on an unfamiliar domain believes the email is safe to give and the reward is real.
angles.cause_addressed: Distrust / legitimacy: an unfamiliar QR-destination page asking for an email BEFORE giving anything reads as a possible scam or spam-trap to a fraction of scanners, who bounce on suspicion.
angles.evidence_hint: QR traffic lands on an unfamiliar domain with a thin, generic trust bar; a share of the ~67% never-engage is consistent with 'looks sketchy, close tab'. Unsettled split (never-engaged vs declined data lands ~Aug) — a bet.
angles.why_untried_and_different: The existing trust bar is boilerplate reassurance; establishing genuine MAKER legitimacy/social proof is a different mechanism, not PR #8's hierarchy rebuild, and not a rejected idea.
angles.on_brand_fit: Handmade-with-love identity is core brand equity; showing the real maker is premium and warm, not pushy.
angles.size: SMALL: swap/augment the trust-bar copy + optional small maker line in claim.html; reversible.

angles.mechanism: Recast '30% off your NEXT order' so it lands for a one-and-done gift buyer who wasn't planning to reorder — anchor it to near-term, giftable relevance ('there's a spud for anybud' → treat someone else / the next occasion) so the discount reads as usable value rather than an irrelevant loyalty perk they'll never redeem.
angles.cause_addressed: Weak/unclear value: the reward is a repeat-purchase discount, and a gift buyer may simply not want a next order — the 'ceiling' hypothesis — so there's nothing worth an email.
angles.evidence_hint: FUNNEL_CONTEXT flags 'they never intended to reorder' as the top competing explanation with a possible ceiling; the offer is explicitly framed as a next-order repeat-purchase. Unsettled — a bet that directly tests the ceiling.
angles.why_untried_and_different: Never reframed; PR #8 changed layout, not the meaning of the offer. It never quotes or compares the printed percentage (not the rejected gap idea) and never gives the code away first (not the rejected discount-first idea).
angles.on_brand_fit: Uses the box's own playful gifting voice; warm, generous framing — on-brand.
angles.size: SMALL: reframe the reward-list copy for the 30% line in claim.html; reversible.

angles.angle: Speak to who actually scanned (giver vs receiver)
angles.mechanism: Add a light, optional acknowledgment of who is holding the phone — the person who was GIVEN the gift vs. the buyer — and let the value speak to each (a receiver just got something lovely; a buyer might reorder). A receiver who scans at unwrapping is not the purchaser, so undifferentiated 'your next order' misfires; naming them keeps them engaged.
angles.cause_addressed: Wrong-audience / timing: the box is on a GIFT, so the scanner is often the recipient, not the buyer, yet the claim page treats everyone identically and pitches a buyer-shaped offer.
angles.evidence_hint: Role (buyer/receiver) is only asked LATER in the create app, meaning the claim page is role-agnostic today; the product is literally a gift, so recipient-scanners are structurally common. Unsettled — a bet.
angles.why_untried_and_different: The claim page has never segmented by audience; this is a new mechanism, not PR #8's structural rebuild, and unrelated to either owner rejection.
angles.on_brand_fit: Warm personal recognition ('this landed with you because someone thought of you') fits the gifting, human tone.
angles.size: SMALL: add one optional acknowledgment line / lightweight two-path copy in claim.html; reversible.

angles.angle: Lead with the video as a second draw
angles.mechanism: Elevate the 'free personalized video starring your crochet friend' from a below-the-fold 'bonus' into a co-equal curiosity hook near the top, so a scanner who doesn't care about a discount still sees a compelling, emotional reason to hand over an email. The email gate stays exactly where it is — the video remains email-delivered — we only give the discount-indifferent a second reason to give it.
angles.cause_addressed: Single-value dependency: if you don't want the discount, the page currently offers nothing you can see fast (the video sits below the form as an afterthought), so a whole segment has zero reason to engage.
angles.evidence_hint: The video is an unannounced bonus not mentioned on the box, currently placed below the email form; the discount-ceiling segment may nonetheless want a keepsake video. Unsettled — a bet.
angles.why_untried_and_different: Distinct from PR #8 (which reorganized the two-reward layout but kept the video as secondary bonus) — this changes which value leads for a specific segment, and crucially does NOT remove or defer the email gate, so it is not the rejected discount-first move.
angles.on_brand_fit: The video is delightful and personal — leaning on it is warm, not pushy, and premium in feel.
angles.size: SMALL/surgical: raise the video's framing + move its caption above the fold in claim.html without removing the form; reversible.

angles.angle: One tap, nothing else (lower the felt cost)
angles.mechanism: For the minority who DO engage, cut the perceived effort/risk of the ask itself: make explicit that it's just an email and nothing more, show the reward is one tap away, and smooth the field interaction so an engaged user doesn't stall or second-guess. Reduces 'engaged-and-gave-up' losses.
angles.cause_addressed: Form friction / felt cost among engagers: typing on a phone, uncertainty about how much they're committing to, or a moment of 'is this worth it' after focusing the field.
angles.evidence_hint: ~33% do engage the field; the never-engaged-vs-declined split isn't measurable until ~Aug, so the size of the declined bucket is unknown. Unsettled — a bet, and by design the smallest-ceiling angle given ~67% never type.
angles.why_untried_and_different: PR #8 restructured the page; this attacks micro-friction/reassurance at the field, a different mechanism, and is neither owner rejection.
angles.on_brand_fit: Quiet, reassuring, low-friction — fits the refined, non-pushy bar.
angles.size: SMALL: reassurance microcopy at the field + minor interaction polish in claim.html; reversible.

pick_rationale: It wins on value × confidence × on-brand fit against the runners-up. The one piece of hard evidence we have — ~67% of scanners never type a single key — says the loss is dominated by people who never ENGAGE, not by form friction, which immediately demotes 'One tap, nothing else' (only reaches the ~33% who engage) and de-risks the whole class of 'first-paint lean-in' angles. Among those, 'Answer the box' targets the most defensible cause of non-engagement: the funnel provably works when the tone is warm (the box's playful voice is what earns the scan in the first place), and the page currently answers that warmth with a cold coupon header — a tonal break we can fix at essentially zero risk. It is the highest on-brand fit by construction (the fix IS the brand voice), the most surgical (one headline + one subhead, instantly reversible), and cleanly distinct from the only thing tried here (PR #8 changed structure, not the opening voice) and from both owner rejections (no printed-% reference, no discount-first). The urgency, trust, value-reframe, audience, and video-hook angles are all genuinely worth the slate, but each is a lower-confidence bet on an unproven cause (ceiling, distrust, audience-mix) that our data can't yet confirm and some carry on-brand risk (honest-urgency can tip pushy). 'Answer the box' has the best expected lift for the least risk and the tightest brand fit, so it is the one to develop first; the planner can pair it with the maker-legitimacy or video-hook angle if a slightly larger swing is wanted.
